title: Equal, no high or low (section 23)
hook: this truth is level; there is nothing high or low in it

segments.voice: Yesterday: nothing gained. In the highest awakening, the Buddha says, not even the least thing is gained. Your line: not the least thing. Did you do one thing without asking what you got out of it? Day one thousand one hundred forty.

A carpenter sets a spirit level on a new shelf. The little bubble drifts, wobbles, and settles dead center between the two lines. Level. Nothing sloping toward one end, nothing tipping the other way. Whatever you set on that shelf will stay where you put it. Section twenty-three of the Diamond Sutra uses a word a carpenter would understand. It says the truth it has been circling is level. Flat. Even. And then it says what that means for anyone who walks on it. Today: equal, no high or low.
screen: `A BUBBLE SETTLES CENTER.` → `NOTHING TIPS.` → `A LEVEL TRUTH.`

segments.voice: First, the word. The Buddha says to Subhuti: this teaching is equal, and there is nothing high or low in it. That is what is called the highest, most complete awakening. The Sanskrit word for equal is sama: same, even, level. Second, the paradox. Notice what just happened. The awakening the sutra keeps calling highest turns out to have no high and no low inside it. It's highest precisely because it isn't a ladder. There's no top rung for someone to stand on while others wait below. Third, how it's reached. The sutra says: without the idea of a self, without the idea of a person, without the idea of a being, without the idea of a life-span, by doing all good things, one awakens. Those four ideas have come up again and again in this sutra. Here they're named again as what has to fall away. Notice it doesn't say do nothing. It says do all good things, just without building a self on top of them. Fourth, the last twist. And these good things, the Buddha adds, are called by the Tathagata not good things; that is why they are called good things. Even goodness isn't allowed to become a rank. The moment good deeds turn into a way of standing higher than someone else, they've stopped being level. In ordinary life we live inside heights: job titles, seating charts, who speaks first at the table, who gets thanked by name. The sutra doesn't pretend those disappear. It says that underneath them, in what's truest, there's nothing to climb. The ground is even all the way across.
screen: `SAMA: EQUAL, LEVEL.` · `HIGHEST, BUT NO LADDER.` · `GOOD DEEDS WITHOUT A SELF.` · `EVEN GOODNESS ISN'T A RANK.` · then, large: `NO HIGH, NO LOW.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice, if you'd like: treat someone as your equal. Settle, and breathe. Bring to mind one person you tend to place above you, someone you defer to. Rest with them a moment, breathing, and let the gap between you level out. Then bring to mind someone you tend to place below you, maybe without meaning to: someone whose name you don't know, or whose opinion you skip past. Rest with them too, and let that gap level out. Two people, one even ground. Breathe with both of them there. The bell holds the time.
Equal. Section twenty-three says this teaching is level, with nothing high or low in it, and that is called the highest awakening. Today's word.
Your line: no high, no low. Today, with one person you usually look up to or look past, speak to them exactly as you'd speak to a friend. Day one thousand one hundred forty.

howItsDone: Mahayana teachers read section 23 as saying awakening holds no ranks: good deeds are done without the ideas of self, person, being or life-span, and without making goodness a way to stand higher.

original.note: Sanskrit and Pali: equal, even, level; section 23 calls the teaching equal.

trapdoor: what you thought: the highest awakening means being above everyone.
what it means: the teaching is level, with nothing high or low, and that is called the highest awakening.
what a scholar hears: the four notions of self, person, being and life-span named again, and 'good things' put through the sutra's not-x pattern.

notes: Section 23 paraphrased, not quoted (Max Müller's wording unverified): check 'this teaching is equal, nothing high or low in it', the four notions (self, person, being, life-span), 'by all good things one awakens', and 'good things are not good things, so called good things'.
Original: sama (सम) as the Sanskrit word for 'equal' in this section; confirm against the Sanskrit text.
The spirit-level image is the writer's, not the sutra's.
